label: Metrically finite populated pasts in every accessible history
definition: PopulatedPastsMetricallyFinite h Concrete k w holds when, in every history v accessible from w, every moment t at which some contingent concrete individual is present has a metrically finite past on the clock k (the readings of moments at or before t are bounded below). In ordinary language: wherever a contingent thing is present in a possible history, only a finite duration of time lies before it. It allows a past with no first moment (open below, as in standard FLRW cosmology) and continuous time with a first moment; it excludes an endless succession of days before a populated moment.
note: Analyst framework definition; attribution deferred. OPEN. Weak version of begun populated pasts in linear time (populatedPastsMetricallyFiniteOfBegun); the converse fails in an open-below finite past (MetricGrimReaper control 2). It does not give a moment with nothing earlier, so it does not by itself feed the A3 prime w derivation.
